newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro bourses slip, dollar edges lower.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro bourses slip, dollar edges lower.

text.p: European bourses slipped in early trading on Tuesday, caught in the slipstream of Wall Street's latest fall, but London and Paris soon traded above their lows.
Frankfurt, down nearly 1.5 percent, showed the biggest fall of major bourses, with weakness of the dollar -- which sours prospects for Germany's many exporters -- a key depressant.
"We have lost what we gained yesterday but volumes are relatively weak. Most players have had enough and just want to celebrate Christmas," said one German share dealer.

"All this volatility is putting people off," said a London trader. "Everybody is very aware that markets are higher than they have ever been before and they're worried about buying at the top, though there's still a lot of cash around."
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar lost a little ground amid caution about prospects for U.S. interest rates and after another shaky performance by U.S. stocks and bonds.

Currency traders were also digesting various pointers to official German views on preferred exchange rate levels in the wake of last week's agreement on a European Union budget stability pact to back up a future single euro currency.
"The main thing underpinning the mark is that it now looks like the Germans are unhappy with the outcome of the EU summit," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
"The French are arguing for political controls over the European central bank and interference in the workings of the single currency system, which is what they got in the stability pact," he said.

New York markets weakened late on Monday as news of a solid 0.9 percent gain for U.S. industrial output last month jangled nerves ahead of a meeting on Tuesday of the the U.S. central bank's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"People seem to be watching the outcome of the FOMC but it's difficult to see any change in rates just yet," said Henry Wilkes, senior trader at Bank Julius Baer.
"No one is expecting a change in rates ahead of Christmas," a London share trader said. "If there is one, it will catch everybody by surprise."

The London stock market, Europe's busiest, opened lower, depressed by a late sell-off in technology stocks in New York which neutralised much of the impact of Boeing's $13.3 billion acquisition of fellow aerospace giant McDonnell Douglas.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 36.52 to 6,268.35, reversing earlier gains. It was up 31 at the London close.
Drug stocks led the way down in London. Traders said investors were still worried about a further slide on Wall Street and the chances of a year-end rally seemed to be fading.
"If there is going to be one (a rally), it will be very, very short-lived," one dealer said. "People will just be pleased if the market hangs on to these levels at the end of the year."

Frankfurt shares also started lower, hit by a weaker dollar and the jolt from Wall Street's reversal. French shares opened down 0.5 percent after New York's slide and ahead of the U.S. central bank meeting but later pared their losses.
"There is really nothing going on, everbody is sitting on their hands," one Paris dealer said.
Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet will later outline the bank's monetary policy goals. Economists expect him to avoid controversy but say he might hint at more rate cuts.

Among currency comments being analysed by the markets, the Bundesbank's latest report said exchange rates broadly reflected fundamental factors and the mark had completely corrected a prolonged period of strength in recent years.
On Monday German finance ministry official Michael Roeskau said a dollar rate of 1.55 marks -- marginally above rates on Tuesday morning -- was one which could be defended on markets.

The German central bank's chief economist, Otmar Issing, told the Financial Times he was not satisfied with a lack of automaticity in the stability pact underpinning planned European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"The dollar's been playing the 1.55-mark level on-and-off lately but it seems to me that people still need a clearer picture of the longer-term implications of the latest EMU developments before taking it higher," said Wilkes.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5465 marks and 113.70 yen, compared with 1.5510 and 114.29 in late business on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of top British shares was down 7.5 at 3,986.3. In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX slid 42.30 to 2,813.49.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 10.86 at 2,211.71.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold rose to a fix of $368.30 an ounce from the previous London close of $367.55. Silver edged up one cent to $4.81.
